lab_title: The Molecular Architecture and Replication of DNA
top_level_objectives: Identify the structural components of the DNA double helix and their chemical orientation.
Explain the mechanism of base-pairing and how it dictates DNA structure.
Describe the function of key enzymes (Helicase, DNA Polymerase, Ligase) in DNA replication.
Distinguish between leading and lagging strand synthesis and explain why they differ.
Articulate the semiconservative model of DNA replication.

scenes.scene_name: The Architecture of the Double Helix
scenes.brief_purpose: Establish the spatial arrangement and chemical composition of the DNA double helix.
key_visuals: A large-scale, interactive double helix model floating in the workspace
Color-coded beads representing phosphate, deoxyribose, and nitrogenous bases
student_actions: Rotate and zoom into the model to identify the sugar-phosphate backbone and the internal base pairs
Tap on individual bases to see labels for Adenine, Thymine, Guanine, and Cytosine

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the chemical basis of base-pairing and antiparallel orientation.
key_visuals: Highlighting of the 5' and 3' ends of the backbones
Visual indicators of hydrogen bond bridges between base pairs
student_actions: Toggle between view modes to visualize the 2-bond (A-T) and 3-bond (G-C) connections
Trace the directionality of the two strands to confirm they run in opposite 5' to 3' orientations

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the initiation of DNA replication at the replication fork.
key_visuals: A stylized Helicase enzyme appearing at a replication origin
The helix beginning to 'unzip' into a replication fork structure
student_actions: Drag the Helicase enzyme along the DNA helix to trigger the unwinding process
Observe Single-Strand Binding Proteins snapping into place to stabilize the parental template strands

scenes.brief_purpose: Explore the continuous synthesis of the leading strand.
key_visuals: DNA Polymerase complex docking onto the 3' end of the leading strand template
A new DNA strand being synthesized in a 5' to 3' direction toward the fork
student_actions: Observe the continuous movement of DNA Polymerase as it synthesizes the leading strand in real-time

scenes.brief_purpose: Understand the challenge of the lagging strand and Okazaki fragments.
key_visuals: A second DNA Polymerase working in the opposite direction of the fork
Discontinuous segments of DNA (Okazaki fragments) appearing on the lagging strand
student_actions: Observe the repeated 'jump-and-synthesize' motion of the Polymerase on the lagging strand template
Identify the gaps between the newly synthesized fragments

scenes.brief_purpose: Finalize the replication process and emphasize semiconservative inheritance.
key_visuals: DNA Ligase enzyme moving to seal the nicks between Okazaki fragments
Two complete double helices highlighting the original 'parental' strands and new 'daughter' strands in different colors
student_actions: Tap the DNA Ligase to finalize the sugar-phosphate backbone connectivity
Compare the two finished double helices to verify that each contains one original and one new strand
